assumptions: Input readings must already be scale-calibrated mGal; raw dial/scale conversion is not inferred. gravity_relative permits zero/negative calibrated relative readings; gravity_observed is positive absolute magnitude. One declared instrument_id and gravity_scale_calibration_id per document.

Declare height_units=m, known height_datum, z_positive=up and permanent tide_system=tide_free/zero_tide/mean_tide. Selected effective datum is metadata.gravity_channel_datums[channel] if present, otherwise metadata.gravity_datum.

Tide application subtracts an explicit externally calculated observed-minus-reference effect for every nonnull selected record ID. Caller verifies its time/position/height and permanent-tide convention. No astronomical, loading, interpolation or permanent-tide transformation is inferred. Tide history and all height/reference reductions must be known unapplied.

Drift requires known applied gravity_tide and known unapplied drift/normal/free-air/Bouguer/terrain. Positive absolute reference values at 2..128 named control records anchor an offset plus piecewise-linear drift in UTC time. Clock/reference comparability is explicitly caller-verified.

Controls are chronologically sorted without reordering observations. Evaluate original source readings at each supplied timestamp; exact knots are supported. Interior predictions require the bracketing interval <=max_gap_seconds; no extrapolation. All nonnull readings and quality bounds must pass before one atomic application.

max_abs_correction_mGal bounds the total bias including any relative-to-absolute datum offset. Adjacent tie bias differences divided by elapsed seconds must satisfy max_drift_rate_mGal_per_s. Output is positive absolute gravity_observed; only the selected per-channel gravity datum is changed.

Consecutive control pairs report closure/delta diagnostics; tie residuals are zero by construction and are not independent validation. This is fixed-reference piecewise-linear loop adjustment, not global network least squares, tare detection or automatic control selection.

Repeat statistics reuse native observation QC and add same-height/comparability flags. Different/missing positions or heights prevent interpreting changes as repeatability; no observations are repaired. Independent non-control repeat stations are used for scientific validation.

Strict supplementary binding covers canonical semantic options/model, instrument/calibration/height/tide/time/station context and drift target datum. Tide effects are offset-datum invariant so subsequent absolute tying does not invalidate them. Generic data bindings preserve geometry/readings/order through subsequent traceable transforms.

All source data/nulls/order/extras/other channels remain; source uncertainty is archived in flat lineage, not propagated. History guards detect accidental edits, not authenticated deliberate rewriting. Existing event/output/workflow limits apply.
binding: SHA-256 UTF-8 compact JSON of [baselode.gravity_temporal_binding.v1,canonical(semantic options excluding event_id/evidence),canonical(model or null),canonical(context),canonical(all [id,time,z,station_id] rows)]. Canonical numbers are [f64,16-digit big-endian IEEE754 hex] with signed zero normalized; lists preserve order; registered ASCII-key objects become sorted [key,canonical(value)] pairs. Drift context includes effective target datum; tide context excludes offset datum.
